data.title: Amino Acid-Dependent mTORC1 Regulation by the Lysosomal Membrane Protein SLC38A9
data.authors: Jung J; Behrends C et al.

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.finding: SLC38A9, a lysosomal membrane protein, mediates amino-acid-dependent mTORC1 activation.
data.abstract_excerpt: The serine/threonine kinase mTORC1 regulates cellular homeostasis in response to many cues, such as nutrient status and energy level. Amino acids induce mTORC1 activation on lysosomes via the small Rag GTPases and the Ragulator complex, thereby controlling protein translation and cell growth. Here, we identify the human 11-pass transmembrane protein SLC38A9 as a novel component of the Rag-Ragulator complex. SLC38A9 localizes with Rag-Ragulator complex components on lysosomes and associates with Rag GTPases in an amino acid-sensitive and nucleotide binding state-dependent manner.

extracted_findings.effect: SLC38A9 is a lysosomal component of the Rag-Ragulator that mediates amino-acid-dependent mTORC1 activation
